newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Rate cut hopes support.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Rate cut hopes support.

text.p: Australian bond spreads mirrored the relatively lacklustre performance of the local market on Monday, as traders waited on the outcome of two key policy meetings this week.
After being flat to slightly wider through the morning session, bonds strengthened in quiet trade through the afternoon with spreads against North American bonds narrowing.
New Zealand bonds failed to carry on with a rally following weak first quarter GDP data, but still improved against local debt on the day.
The main focus for markets remains second guessing the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) and the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC).

The RBA board meets on Tuesday, and is widely expected to sanction an easing of interest rates, while the FOMC meets on Tuesday and Wednesday and is expected to pass on the opportunity to lift U.S. rates.
The local easing has been so well factored into the market that analysts said the risks were skewed to the downside if no change was announced, with a widening of spreads to follow.
However, if the market remained bullish on a rate cutback, pullbacks may be limited as the RBA can ease on any day it chooses, and so may wait until wages and inflation data later this month.
"RBA silence this week may see the domestic market underperform slightly in disappointment," Hambros fixed income economist Su-Lin Ong said.

"Nevertheless the chances of easing will remain significant and together with the moderate growth outlook and excellent inflation prospects, lend support to outperformance in the near term," she said.
